Saints

All Saints

Synaxis of All Saints · Sunday of All Saints

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Hebrews 12:1–2

Revelation 7:9–17

1 Peter 1:15–16

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Orthodox Church in America dedicates the Sunday following Pentecost to all saints, including those known only to God. Its account includes apostles, martyrs, prophets, hierarchs, monastics, and righteous people, joining diverse lives through the work of the Holy Spirit.

[1] Opening two paragraphs

What is depicted

The selected Russian icon, dated 1890, assembles many ranks of haloed saints below a heavenly register. The file description identifies the subject as All Saints. This particular historical composition represents a collective gathering rather than a portrait of one named saint.

[2] File description and displayed historic reproduction

History and tradition

The OCA account cautiously proposes that the feast may have begun as a commemoration of all martyrs and later widened. It also describes the feast’s prominence in the reign of Emperor Leo VI and his wife, Empress Theophano, in the ninth century.

[1] Paragraph beginning This feast may have originated; final two paragraphs

Published explanation

The same account distinguishes confessors from executed martyrs: confessors suffered for their faith without being put to death. It also includes righteous people who attained holiness while living in ordinary society. The categories describe different forms of witness, not one required biography.

[1] Paragraph on Confessors; paragraph on the Righteous

Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

[3] Hebrews 12:1
